description:
Khe's Tech

This mod is almost exclusively hullmods that make fairly big changes to the ships they are used on.
There's also 4 MagicLib Bounties...with one featuring a very painful, challenging and probably unfun fight and its reward being one each of two new ships this mod adds as well as two hullmods.
Then there's another bounty that just lets you claim a gimmick ship, and 3 other bounties that give hullmods.

So, let's start with the hullmods: the reasons for their design vary from 'the vanilla AI about this one thing makes me angry!' to 'what if we turn this particular system on its head?', but also 'what if I did this one part of this hullmod differently?' and 'I like what this other mod does, but what if I do it backwards?'.
These hullmods have varying rarity, but the overall intent is that they are quite rare. You may or may not find them all in a single playthrough.

Here's the list of hullmods and what they do: (wall of text warning):

Spoiler
I've been iterating over balance while testing, to try having at least some semblance of balance. Except for one, none of these hullmods have (nor will have) S-Mod bonuses. All of them can be built in.
Below, I'll be listing each hullmod and the design intent. For simplicity's sake, the hullmod OP costs are 5/10/15/20, except where stated.

Passive Venting Hack: trades active venting for a boost to passive flux dissipation that scales with non-zero venting modifiers. Can't be used on phase (or damper) or shield ships for balance reasons, of course. Also negates zero-flux speed boosts, halves flux capacity, and doubles monthly supply costs.
Design intent: allow ships to use more flux intensive weapons, while alleviating the 'flux lock' problem AI ships get somewhat.
Rolling Nines: +9% to vent rate, automatically forces a vent at 90% flux (unless overloaded), caps overload duration to 9s, but...also multiplies overload duration by 1.9x.
Design intent: Force venting to alleviate flux-lock, but also make overloads somewhat more damning (But not TOO damning). Because the AI sucks at venting sometimes...
Hardflux Shielding Coils: +X% EMP resistance, 1.X mult to phase upkeep cost, X being % of flux capacity taken up by hardflux. Also, hardflux dissipation while shields are active multiplied by zero.
Design intent: this one was pure whimsy, but the idea is you're trading one form of defense for another.
Harmonic Integration Series (Dock only): A set of three hullmods, one for each class of weapon at all sizes: ballistic, energy, and missile. All of these double overload duration.
Costs 0 OP to install. -100 to OP costs of weapon class. Multiplicative increase to flux cost to fire of affected weapons based on the sum of the original OP of all affected weapons. And if it's fluxless? A per-weapon multiplicative penalty to flux dissipation based on OP cost and weapon size (ordered S/M/L). Flux costs: 3%/2%/1%. Fluxless mult values: 1.5%,1.25%,1%.
Design intent: wanting to slot more weapons on ships with a lot of slots and low OP, but not wanting to make it as free as slapping an AI core in and calling it a day.
Artillery Module Series (dock only): Two sets of three, all for large weapons. Unstable, vs normal. Ballistic, Energy, or Missile.
Each one costs 0 OP to install and increases OP costs of affected weapons by (20 for normal, 10 for unstable). The benefit? +1k range to affected weapons. Also have their own flux penalties if the OP costs for affected weapons are brought to zero (such as via Harmonic Integration), which are currently the same as Harmonic Integration's flux modifiers. The unstable version makes the ship overload at 80% flux.
Design Intent: Friend wanted a massively-range boosting hullmod, so I tried to find fitting penalties and catches. Still not sure about this one.
Phase-Warped Anchor (bounty reward, dock only, copies vanilla OP costs): Phase anchor, but no ship limit per encounter. Removes cloak activation cost. Diving costs and requires 2x deployment CR instead of 1x. Also, repairs ship hull percent to match CR percent. Well, mostly (it ends up somewhat less).
Design Intent: Wanted it for the bounty. Ended up making it a reward.
AI Core Fighter Uplink (Dock only): AI ships only, 20% increased Deployment Points of ship and fighters are piloted by a copy of the ship captain (if it is an AI core).
Design Intent: Saw arma and a different carrier mod do it, thought I'd make my own version that's similar but different.
Buttercup Time Reactor (dock only): Reduces timeflow, ship's total timeflow is a damage multiplier. S-Mod Effect: Stronger timeflow reduction.
Design Intent: I saw a mod that does the opposite. Decided to make this. Then realized it needed some kind of balance due to external sources of timeflow because I don't want this to be an easy damage reduction boost.
Phase-Quantum Plating (dock only, no phase/damper/shield ships): Doubles armor, mass, supplies per month and fuel per lightyear. Halves hull integrity, top speed and turn speed. Disables Zero-Flux speed boost.
Design Intent: Slow peanut. Literally it.
Superposition Lens: Triples beam damage (yes I know that's a lot), beam flux cost, and turn rate. Thirds (meaning 1/3 multiplier) beam range and ALL weapon rate of fire.
Design Intent: I got tired of lances missing. So I made this, then threw in drawbacks to force an all-in reckless playstyle with a substantial risk of overloading.
Fighter Defense Extender (dock only): Extends fighter shields, makes fighter phase cloaks cheaper, or just makes them tankier if they dont have either.
Design Intent: Make fighters stronger without buffing damage.
Luddic Torch/Luddic Smite: Ship explosion radius x1.2, increased 0.2 per d-mod. Ship explosion damage x2.5, +0.2 per d-mod. Ship takes 0.83% damage per second until at 1 hp. Ship nearly always recoverable, nearly guaranteed a d-mod. Smite: Turn rate/acceleration x2. Speed/acceleration x1.5. Ship hull repair rate x0.
Design Intent: Ship goes kaboom. For Ludd.
The Otto Shield: Forces shield on at all times, unless venting/overloading. Shield unfold/turn rate x2.
Design Intent: Ever had that one ship or officer that refused to keep their shields up and died because of it?
Otto Phase Coils: Phase activation and upkeep, vent rate and flux dissipation are zero. Zero-Flux available at any level. Ship gains 1% flux per second (special effect). Doubles overload duration, crew losses, D-Mod effects. Increases all weapon OP costs by 300, and weapon malfunction chance by 100%.
Design Intent: For those phase fuel/cargo carriers that you want to escape.
The Otto System: Like the previous Otto hullmods, it's an automation system to take the decision out of your crew's hands, but for ship systems. Shipsystem cooldown is 1.2x faster.
Design Intent: Why not? Plus, it works 'great' on the Spiteful Meteor.
Phase Stasis Coils Series: There are 4 of these, one being from the bounty, and are all mutually exclusive to install. They all share one trait: the timeflow of phasing is basically negated.

Model A: 100% increased upkeep on cloak, but effectively neutralizes the phase speed penalty.
Model B: -50% upkeep cost on phase cloak.
Model C: 100% increased upkeep. simulates timeflow (50% effectiveness) on weapons (turn rate, firing, ammo, repairs) fighters (refits), engine repairs and hull repairs (but not armor). Used to apply to shipsystems but that is too problematic due to snapshotting.
Model O (bounty reward): 100% increased upkeep on cloak, negates speed penalty like model A, and simulates timeflow like model C (but with minimum 1.0 timeflow)

Design intent: trading the speed boost and timeflow on phase ships for more peak performance time. Model O's limit was 'inspired' by a certain RATs ship that massively decreases timeflow on the target of its shipsystem.
Burn Drive Subsystem Series: Currently 4, acquired via bounty. Require Burn Drive, some allow Meteor Drive. May not be installed on ships with shields, damper fields, or phase systems.

They all have an upkeep penalty (currently 1.5x), a shipsystem cooldown penalty (2.0x base, but scales down the more are equipped), and prevent weapons from firing while active. Unless there's more than one equipped, they all overload the ship when burn drive ends after fully spooling up and negate flux dissipation while the burn drive is active, or when the ship overloads after reaching full spool.
Meteor:  While active grants invulnerability and multiplies mass by 13. Causes flameout at the end unless more than one subsystem. Usable with Burn Drive or Meteor Drive.
Phasediver: Ship enters phase at full spool, gaining 15x timeflow per subsystem. Burn drive only.
Red-Glare: Reloads 10% or 1, whichever is higher, ammo for all equipped weapons, multiplied by subsystem count. Massively increases weapon repair time while overloaded, or instantly repairs all weapons if more than one subsystem. Causes flameout at the end if only one subsystem. Usable with Burn Drive or Meteor Drive.
Lightwave: Multiplies top speed and acceleration by 2x, +1x per subsystem (so 3x at base). Massively increases engine repair time while overloaded, or instantly repairs all engines if more than one subsystem. Causes flameout at the end unless more than one subsystem. Burn Drive only, and only on destroyers or frigates with less than 1k mass.

Design intent: I like ramming ships. Then I went crazy.

Since I added new shipsystems for a few of the ships, here they are:

Spoiler

Phase-Quantum Disruptor: like quantum disruptor, but -25% of base flux 'cost' instead of 25%. Usable while cloaked, but exits cloak while doubling the cloak cooldown. When used on cloaked ships, overloads them for 3s instead of 1s.
Phase-Warp Cloak: Phase cloak, but: a longer cooldown than 2 (9s, so 4.5s with field modulation. half these for the fighters.). Ship also dumps hardflux up to 10% of maximum flux when exiting cloak, and has 1.2x flux dissipation while the system is on cooldown.
Meteor Drive: Burn drive, with much higher speed (it was able to reach around 400-500), no chance to flame out, and a significantly longer cooldown (20s). Also disables venting, turning, weapon use, etc. Once it starts, there is no stopping it.

Then the new ships, with a warning: it's got ultra-ultra-redacted stuff.

Spoiler
Side-attraction, a blue and red skinned Vanguard variant. Spiteful Meteor. Doubled the base DP, and also reduced its max OP and slightly reduced the base flux dissipation (-10).
Has built in rugged like the base version. Also has high maintenance, rolling 9s, passive vent hack, phase-quantum armor, heavy armor, shield shunt, and Meteor Drive Subsystem paired with the Meteor Drive ship system.

Three blue painted ships:
The Diveslaught, an Onslaught with built-in shield shunt and Phasediver subsystem.
A Firecracker Legion with built-in shield shunt and Red-Glare subsystem.
A Lightwave Berserker with built-in Lightwave subsystem.

Ultra ultra redacted stuff:
Inverted color and horizontally flipped Tesseract and Facet. Neither splits on death. Both are obtained from the bounty (1 of each). Both have doubled fuel and supply costs (and sensor profile) if crewed by a non-core captain. Both automatically purge D-Mods. Both had their OP capacity reduced based on the built-in hullmods.
All phase ships listed here use Phase-Warp Cloak.
Phase-Warped Tesseract:
Phase carrier, built-in wings. Yes, you read that right. Phase. Carrier. Tesseract. Comes with built-in Defensive Targeting Array, AI Core Fighter Uplink, Phase-Warped Anchor, and model O phase stasis coils. Has Quantum Disruptor ship system.
The Iotas this deploys are equipped with shock repeaters and Point Defense AI. They can't leave the ship, but they're also phase ships.
Phase-Warped Facet:
Another omega carrier, but not a phase ship. Instead, it has Phase-Quantum Plating, Shield Shunt, Passive Venting Hack and AI Core Fighter Uplink built in. And a Damper Field.
Its fighters, unlike the tesseract, are damage oriented. They have Superposition Lens and Rift Lances. Obnoxious deathsqitos from a slow ship.

Lastly, the bounties, and again: the ultra redacted one is very painful and probably very unfun and, as a result, subject to change. You were warned.

Spoiler
bounty 1: Destroy the Ugly Vanguard: level 5+ and 90+ days at a pirate market. pirate vs pirate. decent size fleet but mostly just autogenerated, other than the spiteful meteor (a heavily modified and over-modded Strike Vanguard variant that happens to sport The Otto System).

bounties 3,4,5: similar to bounty 1, but levels 7,9,11 at 180, 360 and 720 days. bounty 5 also requires defeating a remnant fleet. Progressively increasing fleet scaling and quality, but still pirates until bounty 5 which is remnant with 3 guaranteed Radiants to fight.

Bounty 2: the ultra redacted one. with a silly name.
Unlocked by beating an Omega fleet, being level 10+ and having spent 1 cycle in the sector.
vanilla ships:
1 Strike Tesseract, 1 Assaulter Tesseract, 1 Attack Facet, 1 Attack 2 Facet,
custom ships, basically using somewhat modified vanilla versions of the vanilla configs unless stated:
1 Strike Warped Tesseract, 1 Assaulter Warped Tesseract,
1 Strike Warped Facet, 1 Peanut Warped Facet (heavy armor, PDAI, and reinforced bulkheads)
And the Fleet Commander: 1 Disruptor Warped Tesseract.

All captained by the fleet commander, who has all elite combat skills.
Beating the fleet yields 1 AI Core (the commander's), the 2 mentioned hullmods and the 2 mentioned ships.

Technical notes/(In)Compatibility:

Mod includes special cleanup code for the timeflow hullmods in this mod, because vanilla doesn't have that (while some mods necessitate it). If you've ever had 'stuck' timeflow, you know what I mean. Other mod authors are free to implement their own versions of this.
AI Core Fighter Uplink is a fighter captain replacer. Naturally only one will apply. Examples: Armaa's Overlord Suite series of hullmods or WINGCOM suite, RATs' Autonomous Bays Alteration, Postmodern Carriers' Avatar Core. CROSS-MOD CRASH NOTE: Any of these will induce a crash if copying Knights of Ludd's Dusk superboss AI core onto a fighter that does not have a phase system, at least until they update their live branch.
prv/UGH - extreme phase-modifying hullmods. No idea how well they'll work with the Otto Phase hullmod. Use at own risk. Phasic Armor Frame from UGH prevents phase anchors from protecting the ship during dive.
Realistic Combat, Second in Command: lol, probably not compatible?
Knights of Ludd: there is a specific boss core that is 'tuned for quantum disruptor usage'. do not, under any circumstances, use it on the phase warped tesseract (or any other phase carrier with AI Core fighter uplink) until KoL fixes it on their end. it will crash you to desktop in combat.
Arma Armatura special mention: mod does not use nullchecks much and does a lot of things differently. If something breaks and the stacktrace mentions armaa? Not my problem.

Plans:

Uh...no, I don't do 'plans'.

Changelog:

Spoiler

1.1.1: revised 3 vulnerable hullmods to verify the existence of phase/shipsystem/shield during runtime.
1.1.0: 3 new ships, 3 new bounties, 3 new hullmods (burn drive series) and a rework of a prior one
1.0.3: Specially Treated Doritos now have High Maintenance. Revised some tooltips. Changed Harmonic Integration to higher penalties the smaller a weapon is.
1.0.2: fixed a typo in a hullmod desc. spiteful meteor bounty ship now features the new hullmod: The Otto System. Implemented The Otto System. bounty is now an obliteration. revised bounty meteor's hullmods.
1.0.1: meteor drive subsystem removed as a drop, whoops
1.0: Initial public release.

Thanks/Resources:

Entire Star Sector team for making da game in da first place.
Alex: for answering many questions, and for the API call that makes the inverted phase anchor able to provide hull restoration
Whoever sprited the SUPER ALABASTER ships. Shiny.
Protonus: because they made the Jandor Time Reactor, which the buttercup started as a direct opposite to...except it doesnt affect fighters and now functions differently.
A bugfriend, for da gift of da game.
